text:
maria: Heads-up — I'm sketching changes to the forecasting pipeline so we capture region/network signals + preemptible GPU hours. Current model treats clusters as monoliths and misses: network egress spikes, zone-level throttles, and preemptible churn. We need these to improve capacity planning for seasonal demand.

ajay: Agree. We only aggregate at cluster_id today. Adding region and provider_zone tags + a preemptible flag makes sense. Also want per-request latency buckets (p50/p95) to correlate with load.

devon: Quick note — we should keep rolling 5m and 1h aggregates. For forecasting, 5m helps detect bursty events (eg: egress storms) while 1h smooths for trend models.

katie: Can we also include a boolean for "degraded_network" from the network-monitoring alerts? That signal could explain sudden GPU underutilization. cc @maria :eyes: 

maria: Yeah. Proposal: extend usage_events with fields: region, provider_zone, preemptible (bool), network_egress_bytes, degraded_network_tag, request_queue_len. Example schema & sample queries below — fat-fingered but should be enough to implement.

maria: ```sql
-- new usage_events schema (proposal)
CREATE TABLE usage_events (
  event_ts TIMESTAMP,
  org_id STRING,
  cluster_id STRING,
  region STRING,
  provider_zone STRING,
  model STRING,
  gpu_type STRING,
  preemptible BOOL,
  gpu_seconds FLOAT,
  tokens_generated INT,
  latency_p50_ms INT,
  latency_p95_ms INT,
  network_egress_bytes BIGINT,
  degraded_network BOOL,
  request_queue_len INT
);
```

ajay: Thanks — two operational asks: 1) metric retention: keep raw events for 90 days, aggregates for 2 years. 2) Backfill plan for last 12 months (best-effort) so seasonal model gets training data. Backfill will be best-effort for preemptible flag (we only started logging it last qtr).

devon: For pipeline: Kafka topic `usage-events-v2` (partition by region) -> stream processor that writes to clickhouse (5m/1h materialized) -> daily aggregate job for forecasting features. Also we should publish a small change log when schema evolves (avoid consumer breaks).

maria: Example feature-extraction SQL to feed the forecaster:
```sql
SELECT
  date_trunc('hour', event_ts) AS hour,
  region,
  SUM(gpu_seconds)/3600.0 AS gpu_hours,
  AVG(latency_p95_ms) AS p95_latency_ms,
  MAX(network_egress_bytes) AS peak_egress,
  SUM(CASE WHEN preemptible THEN gpu_seconds ELSE 0 END)/3600.0 AS preemptible_gpu_hours,
  AVG(request_queue_len) AS avg_queue_len
FROM usage_events
WHERE event_ts >= now() - interval '90 days'
GROUP BY 1,2;
```

katie: Dashboards: Add these panels to capacity forecasting dashboard (by region): gpu_hours, preemptible_share, p95_latency, peak_egress, degraded_network rate, queue_len. Also add a small seasonality viz (weekday x hour heatmap). :chart_with_upwards_trend: 

infra-bot: [alert] deploy:usage-ingest v2 -> staging succeeded for 3 partitions.

sre-ops: Note — when we partition by region, we should watch uneven partition sizes. ap-southeast tends to be small but bursty; us-west is huge. We may need weighted sampling in the forecaster or more partitions for busy regions.

ajay: Cost signal: add `preemptible_gpu_hours * price_preemptible + non_preemptible_gpu_hours * price_on_demand` to daily aggregates so finance can compare unit economics. We should also track egress cost by region.

maria: Action items: 1) ajay + devon to draft schema migration + backfill plan (ETA 48h). 2) infra -> prod Kafka topic and partitioning plan. 3) devex/docs: update schema doc + example queries. 4) katie -> add panels to dashboard and heatmap. I'll start a PR with the proposed schema and a small consumer that tags preemptible.

katie: I'll mock a heatmap and embed in the dashboard prototype by EOD.

devon: I'll add a consumer that writes `degraded_network` when network-monitoring alerts coincide with spikes. Will instrument and run in staging first.

maria: Thanks all — if we can get the backfill & schema in flight this week, we can retrain the seasonal forecaster next week and test how much accuracy improves with region/egress signals.

ajay: one more: consider adding model-specific qps (requests/min per model) so we can do per-model capacity plans for hot models. low-priority but useful.

maria: Noted. We'll add that to the follow-up backlog. :white_check_mark:
